text: Gotham Central Bank. Ten bags, one night, zero witnesses. Are you in or out? Choose fast, I bill by the hour.
Alley's clear. Well, clear of people. The rats have formed a union.
Tap Space to ping. Hold it for a bigger one. Bigger pings feel great and get you arrested. Your call.
Sneak with Ctrl. Quiet feet, quiet life.
Guard ahead. Don't wave.
Nap time. Very professional.
His pager's going off. Answer it, or he's about to get very popular.
Well. That's the sound of someone noticing.
Red keycard. Finally, something in this city that works.
Cameras are looping. Two minutes. I know their blind spots like, well, never mind.
Power's off at the vault gate. Which means it opens. Which means you should.
Lasers. Of course. Why would a bank have a normal door? Ping before you step.
That's the alarm. That's... okay, that's loud. Okay! Plan B! I love Plan B! Thermite, now!
Police in thirty seconds. Okay, twenty. They're early. Rude.
Thermite's burning. Hold the door. Or the hall. Or anything.
Vault's open. Beautiful. Grab the bags before the dye packs get ideas.
Vault's open and nobody noticed. I'd clap, but I'm busy being impressed.
Dye packs are armed. Disarm them or enjoy pink money.
Heavy, isn't it? Money usually is. Keep moving.
Bollards are down. Van's on its way. Try to look like a delivery.
Van's here. Bags in, you in, everyone out.
Fun fact: I'm the bank's night dispatcher. Eleven years, same cameras, same salary. Consider this my resignation. I quit.
That went poorly. Rewinding. Please don't do that again.
You're leaking. Heal, or become a cautionary tale.
No alarm. No witnesses. I'm genuinely moved.
